item.title: A proof of the Nevo-Peeva conjecture: Exact regularity and linear powers of gap-free edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.33501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with at least one edge, and let $I(G)$ be its edge ideal over a field $K$. We prove that if $G$ is gap-free, then $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q=\max\{2q,\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)+q-1\}$ for all $q\geq 1$. This answers both open problems of Nevo and Peeva on ordinary powers: $I(G)^q$ has a linear resolution exactly when $q\geq \mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, and their proposed regularity recurrence holds with equality. As consequences, the upper bound $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)^q\leq 2q+\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-2$ conjectured by Alilooee, Banerjee, Beyarslan, H\`a, Jayanthan and Selvaraja holds for gap-free graphs; every power $I(G)^q$ with $q\geq 2$ has a linear resolution when $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)=3$; and the stabilization index equals $\mathrm{reg}\, I(G)-1$, which is unbounded on this class. The proof rests on a combinatorial result of independent interest: a parity-sensitive homology vanishing theorem for a filtration of the independence complex by a weighted Hall defect. An internalization lemma and sublevel complexes of submodular functions control the local terms, and Hall's theorem together with an implication-digraph argument classifies the zero level. A capacitated form of the Tutte-Berge formula and Takayama's formula identify the filtration with the degree complexes of ordinary powers. The algebraic statements hold over every field, and the topological vanishing holds with arbitrary abelian coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Luis Alfredo Dupont Garc\'ia

item.title: Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings, with applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33994v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings and give applications to rational double points and perfectoid towers. We realize rational double points of ADE over $W(k)$ as invariant subrings $A^G$, where $A$ is a ramified two-dimensional complete regular local ring and $G$ is a finite linearly reductive subgroup scheme of $\mathrm{SL}_{2,W(k)}$. We also prove a general theorem on the existence of Frobenius lifts on invariant subrings: if a flat affine group scheme $G$ over $W(k)$ admits a functorial Reynolds operator and a relative Frobenius lift, then any formal power series ring equipped with a linear action of $G$ admits a Frobenius lift that restricts to a Frobenius lift on the invariant subring. Building on these results, we construct perfectoid towers arising from rational double points in mixed characteristic. We identify their tilts with the perfect towers arising from rational double points in positive characteristic of the same ADE type.
item.dc:creator: Kazuki Hayashi

item.title: A lower bound on levels with applications to Koszul complexes
item.description: arXiv:2505.14812v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we establish a lower bound on the level of a perfect complex with $I$-power torsion homology on positive degrees and an $I$-power torsion minimal generator for zeroth homology. Examples are provided to demonstrate that the bound is optimal. This result is applied to improve existing lower bounds on the level of a Koszul complex on various classes of sequences.
item.dc:creator: Antonia Kekkou

item.title: The $i$-extended ideal-based cozero-divisor graph of a commutative ring
item.description:
arXiv:2605.05237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let R be a commutative ring with identity and let J be an ideal of R. In this paper, we introduce and investigate the notion of the i-extended ideal-based cozero-divisor graph of R. This graph, denoted by $\overline{\Gamma''}_{Ji}(R)$, is a simple graph of R whose vertex set is ${x \in R \ J : xR + J 
ot= R}$. Two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ are adjacent if and only if $x^m 
ot \in y^nR+J$ and $y^n 
ot \in x^mR+J$ for some positive integers m and n with $n\leq i$ and $m\leq i$.
item.dc:creator: Faranak Farshadifar

item.title: On $F$-thresholds of differential power filtrations
item.description: arXiv:2607.09028v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the $F$-threshold of differential power filtrations of monomial ideals. We give the existence of this number and show that it is upper bounded by the maximum height of the minimal primes of the underlying monomial ideal. As an application of our results, we show that the dimension of the polynomial ring and the $F$-threshold of the differential power filtration of the monomial maximal ideal are the same.
item.dc:creator: W\'agner Badilla-C\'espedes

item.title: Persistent Bass and Lyubeznik Numbers of Stanley Reisner Rings
item.description: arXiv:2611.26813v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define persistent Lyubeznik numbers and persistent Bass numbers of Stanley--Reisner rings along a simplicial filtration. For Lyubeznik numbers we show that the complex of \`Alvarez Montaner and Vahidi computing $\lambda_{p,q}(\kk[\Delta])$ is natural for inclusions of simplicial complexes, so that persistent Lyubeznik numbers are ranks of maps on its cohomology. We give an equivalent costar complex, whose terms are reduced homology groups of links of faces and whose differentials are induced by quotient maps; it requires neither Alexander duals nor free resolutions. For Bass numbers at coordinate primes we prove that the Hochster-type formula is natural for inclusions, which identifies the persistent Bass numbers with the persistent graded Betti numbers of Suwayyid and Wei for filtered links. Both families have finite barcodes and satisfy bottleneck stability. Examples, including two isomers with the same persistent homology, exhibit Lyubeznik bars that persistent homology does not detect.
item.dc:creator: Kaiyue He, Faisal Suwayyid, Guo-Wei Wei

item.title: A Note on Binary Quadratic Systems and their relation to complexity theory
item.description: arXiv:2609.07769v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deciding whether a system of multivariate quadratic equations over $\mathbb F_2$ has a solution is a classical NP-complete problem, and remains so for square systems, with as many equations as variables. The hardness of this problem is one of the cornerstones of nowadays post-quantum cryptography. Let $\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ and $\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ denote the sets of square quadratic systems in $n$ variables having respectively no solutions and exactly one solution. $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_0(n)$ is a coNP-complete language, while $\cup_{n\geq 2} \mathrm{MQ}_1(n)$ lies in DP. It is known that $\lim_{n\to \infty} |\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)|/|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|=1$. Here we prove the explicit finite-$n$ bounds \[ |\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|<|\mathrm{MQ}_1(n)| \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)|\mathrm{MQ}_0(n)|, \] More generally, let $Q_d$ be the space of polynomial functions $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n\to\mathbb F_2$ of degree at most $d$, and let $\alpha_k$ count square systems in $(Q_d)^n$ having exactly $k$ solutions. Then \[ \alpha_0<\alpha_1 \le \left(1+\frac{1}{2^n-1}\right)\alpha_0\,, \qquad 2\le d\le n \,. \] The proof combines matroid and coding-theoretic methods. We interpret $(\mathbb{F}_2)^n$ as the ground set of the evaluation matroid of $Q_d$, express $\alpha_0$ and $\alpha_1$ through characteristic polynomials, and use a Whitney-type sign-reversing involution to show that the only terms that can push $\alpha_1-\alpha_0$ below $\alpha_1/2^n$ come from the elements of a matroid port. These are identified with minimal-support words of the Reed--Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(n-d-1,n)=\mathrm{RM}(d,n)^\perp$; the required estimate then follows from the MacWilliams identity, the minimum-distance bound $2^{d+1}$, and the even-weight structure of the code.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Radici, Massimiliano Sala
